summary: Listed as a Dare County, NC tower named Hatteras Inlet CG; no source read describes the tower itself or its current state.

facts.status_note: The NGS listing codes the survey mark as a surface mark reported destroyed; no source read describes the tower's own status.

events.note: Life-Saving Service station on Ocracoke Island, near the inlet; sources disagree on its site. About the station, not the tower.
The 1883 station was demolished and a new Coast Guard station was built at the inlet. About the station, not the tower.
Crew evacuated to Hatteras Island on 3 October 1951 after erosion made the Coast Guard station unsafe in storms. About the station, not the tower.

notes_for_editor: The only sources that name the tower are the tnlandforms index and the NGS datasheet listing, and neither describes the structure. The station history is about the Coast Guard station and is labelled as such; no source read ties a tower to the 1883 or 1917 station. The sources disagree on the 1883 station's site (Ocracoke north end near Hatteras Inlet versus the Hatteras side, per the Chamber's 'Hatteras Inlet (1883)' entry); the story says so. The NGS listing has two rows for the mark (codes XX and NN, in the horizontal and vertical nonpub fields). The USCG station history page returned HTTP 403 and the NC Digital Collections item has no readable text, so neither is used. The 1962 date for the present station appeared only in a search summary and is not used. facts.agency ('U.S. Coast Guard') and facts.access ('restricted') were removed: no source read states an agency or public access for the tower; the 'CG' in the name is the only hint and the story does not claim more. The summary no longer says the tower is 'named for' the station, which is an inference. Body text is about 238 words, longer than the 120-word thin-source length because the station history fills most of it; that history is labelled as station history, not tower history.
